name: webgpu-page-transition
title: WebGPU Page Transition
description: Image planes that morph between three views on one WebGPU canvas: a looping carousel, a draggable 3D float and a detail stack, with masked text reveals; WebGL 2 or plain images as fallbacks.
label: bnpne WebGPU page transitions
author: Ben Paine <https://github.com/bnpne>

props.name: images
props.type: { src: string; alt?: string; width: number; height: number; caption?: string; fact?: string }[]
props.description: The images (five in the original). width and height set each slot's aspect ratio; the caption names its carousel button; the fact is the detail view's paragraph. Read on mount: key the component to swap the set.

props.name: view / defaultView / onViewChange
props.description: The view: the carousel, the 3D index, or one image's detail stack. Controlled with view and onViewChange, or uncontrolled from defaultView. A view chosen during a transition applies when it ends.

props.name: labels
props.type: { main?: string; index?: string; inner?: string; nav?: string }
props.description: The views' names (the navigation and the title in the corner) and the navigation's accessible name.

props.name: intro
props.description: Fade the planes in and reveal the text once the canvas is ready.

props.name: forceWebGL
props.description: Draw with WebGL 2 even where WebGPU is available.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level of the view titles.

a11y: Views switch with real buttons: the navigation (aria-current on the active view), one button per carousel image named by its caption, and on the index view a list of buttons (shown on focus) to open each image.
Arrow keys move the carousel by one image and spin the index float; the detail view's scroll area is focusable.
Split text keeps its words or lines aria-hidden with a visually hidden copy of the whole text, so screen readers read it once.

Without WebGPU three.js draws with WebGL 2; without either, and under prefers-reduced-motion, the images are plain DOM (alt text, rounded corners), views cut or crossfade and nothing tilts or floats on its own.
The canvas pauses off screen and in hidden tabs (render-loop), with its pixel ratio capped at 2. The secondary text is 50% opacity as upstream; under prefers-contrast: more it is full opacity.
usage: <WebGPUPageTransition className="h-svh" images={[{ src: "/a.jpg", width: 4, height: 5, caption: "First", fact: "About the first image." }]} />
